$comment: TechDocs/POS_OPENCORE.md §11 — what the public mirror receives (open-core, step O-6).
The private monorepo is the source of truth; `export.mjs sync` replays its `main` onto the public repository, minus everything that is not PUBLIC here.
Patterns: `dir/` = everything under it; anything else = one file, where `*` stands for part of ONE path segment.

A path is PRIVATE if any `private` pattern (or one derived from pos/private-modules.json) matches it; else PUBLIC if a `public` pattern matches it; else UNKNOWN — and an unknown path fails `export.mjs check`, so nothing new is published or withheld by default.

`explicit` directories ask for more: a path under one is public only through a pattern that is more specific than the directory itself, so every child is listed by name (`pos/` being public does not make a new `pos/src/modules/<dir>` public).
`rename` publishes a file under another name (the public CLAUDE.md is CLAUDE.public.md here; the full CLAUDE.md stays private).
Derived from pos/private-modules.json for every private module id: `pos/src/modules/<id>/`, `pos/vite.<id>-remote.config.ts`, `pos/e2e/<id>.spec.ts`.
bootstrapMessage:
Open-core: online modules move to a private repository

The sources of the online-only modules (the flowers, café and grocery verticals, tables, debts, the TikTok LIVE desk and the ПРРО cabinets) and their design documents are no longer published here. The platform, the backend and the bundled modules stay open under the OwnNet Source License 1.1, and a store keeps running on them alone: the clothing vertical ships in the host, and anyone can write modules of their own against @pos/platform.

From this commit on this repository is an automatic export of the open part; earlier history is unchanged.
